inline_comments.comment: The default parameter `maxPresetColors = 27` only applies when the caller passes `undefined`. When `ColorControl` passes the raw prop value from `ColorConfig`, an explicitly set `NaN` or negative number bypasses this default and reaches the hook as-is. Consider normalising/validating the value inside `usePresets` itself (or at the call site before passing it in) rather than relying solely on the default parameter, so the 27-fallback is actually exercised for all invalid inputs.

Neither `WithMaxPresetColors` nor `WithUnlimitedPresetColors` has a `play` function. For `WithMaxPresetColors` in particular, adding a `play` function that queries color swatch elements and asserts exactly 5 are rendered (not all 8 provided) would give this feature automated regression protection. Without it, a future refactor that breaks the limiting logic would go undetected.

The JSDoc documents `0` and `Infinity` as "unlimited" sentinels but is silent on what happens when the caller passes a negative number or `NaN`. Once the validation logic is corrected (see comment on `Color.tsx`), the JSDoc should describe the fallback: something like `@remarks Negative values and NaN are treated as invalid and fall back to the default of 27.` This prevents callers from discovering the behaviour only at runtime.

general_comments.comment: The CodeRabbit-generated PR summary mentions a third story "showing fallback behavior for an invalid negative setting," but no such story exists in the diff or in the codebase. Since the current implementation handles negative `maxPresetColors` incorrectly (it produces the wrong slice rather than a graceful fallback), this missing story represents a gap in both coverage and documentation. Once the validation bug is fixed, a story (or unit test for `usePresets`) exercising negative, `NaN`, and non-integer float inputs would confirm the fallback to 27 and provide a permanent regression guard.
